cells.tense: Right now the form you willed into being is nearly standing, and you are holding it steady rather than forcing the last push.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Work the thing you're closest to finishing from your own reserves for one focused stretch — no updates, no checking how it lands — then set it down when the stretch ends.
cells.core:
You can carry a thing through pressure on your own fuel. Nothing here has been settled yet, every direction still open, and you are standing in that openness with enough internal weight to keep moving without anyone holding the other end. The finish you are capable of is quiet.

Notice what holding looks like. Keeping going without checking on anyone is not the same as shoving the thing over the line — it is a span of time where you sustain it from what you have and count that as the work. Openness is not an obstacle. It is the material you are finishing from.

cells.verb: to carry a form through to completion by sustained will

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the finished thing to land, planning how it will read, before any of it exists.
cells.ask: Let something arrive this week with no plan waiting for it. No outline, no outcome already decided. Take it as it comes and stop there for now.
cells.core:
When the pull is toward completion, the pull runs past the moment. You want the end already standing, so you brace for it, shape it in advance, defend a finish that does not exist yet. Where every direction is still open, bracing is the one move the ground cannot hold.

The way back is not less work — it is taking what has not arrived yet. Receive something unprepared and let its next part come without you deciding its shape. That is not passive. It lets the openness do its work, so the finish you eventually push for is one you chose rather than one you outran.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things before they've started.

cells.tense: You stood at the edge of something that could have been completed, and you are still there now that the door is behind you.
cells.ask: Once, watch whatever is nearest you for a minute, no naming yet. Then say what you saw — no judgment, no comparison, no moving to the next task.
cells.core:
The whole of this ability is in you; what went quiet is the place it lands. Somewhere before, there was a thing you could have carried to completion, and you are still at the threshold. That is not a judgment about what happened. It is only where the work sits now: at a door that has closed.

Seeing has to charge before anything gets built. Watch what is actually before your eyes before naming what it might mean, and make the watching the whole of the effort. Not a plan, not a return. Just that first look, small, where you are. It refills what the building runs on.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at a door that closed behind you.

cells.tense: You are the one bringing the form through to completion, and if someone asked, you would say it had nothing to do with you.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Name one finished thing near you — something that holds because you keep it holding — and write how it looks today, plainly, with no explanations and no credit.
cells.core:
You can bring something all the way to standing, and when it stands, the making of it drops out of the account. Look at what holds around you — the arrangements, the finished work, the thing that runs because you keep it running. Some of it got there through your sustained will, and the telling you give is that it happened without you. The one who carried it is left out of the story.

Bringing that back takes nothing grand. Write the plain lines of a finished thing, no conclusion, no credit, and leave them as they are. Whoever wrote those lines made the thing.
cells.sheetLine: You built the standing thing and don't say so.
